methodology.description: Public draft-helper PPR redraft board. Player value and market cost are intentionally kept separate. Rankings blend broad expert consensus, current projections, recent independent expert boards and material preseason/news context; ADP is treated as price rather than player quality. League scoring, roster construction, draft slot, drafted players, positional scarcity and next-pick pressure are applied by the client recommendation engine.
rankingInputs: FantasyPros 2026 PPR consensus, injury feed and current market data checked Sept. 3
ESPN Sept. 3 draft guide, Aug. 31 final PPR mock and current fantasy news
RotoWire Sept. 3 PPR rankings, health reports and player news
CBS Sports current analyst boards, injury coverage and ADP context checked Sept. 3
NFL.com official injury/transaction reporting checked through Sept. 3
Rotoworld/NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Fantasy Life and other independent market sources checked through Sept. 3
methodology.marketInput: Current PPR ADP remains a separate market-price input, cross-checked across RotoWire, FantasyPros, Sleeper-market samples, CBS/Yahoo and other platform references. ADP is not used as a substitute for player value; large gaps remain when injury, availability, role uncertainty or expert disagreement justifies them.
newsInputs: Ja'Marr Chase remains No. 3, but confidence is reduced. He was present but did not participate in Wednesday practice after the recent left-knee hyperextension. Cincinnati still says it feels good about his progress, and fresh PPR boards continue to rank him at or near No. 3 overall, so this is an uncertainty adjustment rather than a talent downgrade.

Ashton Jeanty remains No. 23, with confidence reduced slightly. He worked off to the side Tuesday but remained out of practice Wednesday. The injury is believed to be a low-ankle sprain and Las Vegas still expects him to have a chance for Week 1, while RotoWire's Sept. 3 PPR board ranks him No. 19. The public board therefore preserves the market/value discount without overreacting to one missed session.

Jeremiyah Love moves from No. 24 to No. 26. Arizona says he is progressing well from the high-ankle sprain, but he still had not returned to drills as of Tuesday. RotoWire's Sept. 3 PPR board also has him No. 26, so the small downgrade better reflects current availability risk while keeping his upside range intact.

MarShawn Lloyd moves from No. 65 to No. 74. ESPN's final PPR mock took him 70th after the Josh Jacobs news, while RotoWire's Sept. 3 season-long PPR board is much more cautious at No. 98. Lloyd remains the favorite to lead Green Bay's backfield while Jacobs is unavailable, but the first post-news market spike was too aggressive to treat as settled season-long value.

Josh Jacobs moves from No. 82 to No. 90. He remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List and cannot practice or play while listed. ESPN's final PPR mock let him fall to 87th and RotoWire's Sept. 3 PPR board has him 94th, so the fresh cross-source center is lower than yesterday's file despite the possibility that he returns later in the season.

Puka Nacua remains No. 4. RotoWire still lists him questionable with a groin issue but expects a Sept. 10 return, and current top-five valuation remains intact. No fresh evidence justified another rank change today.
methodology.notes: Expert disagreement is preserved with expertHigh/expertLow ranges; unresolved injuries, discipline risk and genuine model disagreement can intentionally widen those ranges. Confidence reflects agreement plus news certainty, not ceiling. This file is used only by smhillis/sleeper-draft-helper-public and must not be copied into or used to modify Scott's personal Sleeper Draft Assistant.
